findings.source_quote: Θεῷ τῷ κτίσαντι τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὸ σύμπαν οὐ λείπει πρόφασις πρὸς σωτηρίαν τῶν σώζεσθαι θελόντων.
findings.english_quote: God, who created heaven and the universe, lacks no means for the salvation of those who wish to be saved.
findings.issue: “Means” gives the general practical sense but obscures the framing of πρόφασις as an occasion or grounds for action, repeated later in προφάσει τῆς τοῦ σώματος θεραπείας. The note lists possible senses without explicitly comparing these linked occurrences. “Does not lack an occasion” is the more source-transparent candidate.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “God, who created heaven and the universe, does not lack an occasion for the salvation of those who wish to be saved.” Explicitly document the repeated πρόφασις wording and the contextual reason for rendering its later occurrence “pretext.”

findings.source_quote: ὅθεν μηδὲ ἐπὶ τοῖς δοκοῦσιν φαύλοις ὑπὸ προπετείας τις αὐτὸν ὡς μὴ φιλάνθρωπον αἰτιάσθω.
findings.english_quote: Therefore, no one, through rashness, should accuse him of lacking benevolence toward humanity on account of things that appear bad.
findings.issue: The negation is retained, but μηδὲ gives the circumstances an “even” emphasis: God should not be accused even on account of apparently bad things. That emphasis is absent.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “Therefore, no one should rashly accuse him of lacking benevolence toward humanity, even on account of things that appear bad.”

findings.source_quote: οὐ θέλεις τὴν σὴν ὑφ’ ἑτέρου μοιχευθῆναι γυναῖκα, τὴν ἑτέρου μὴ μοίχευε γαμετήν
findings.english_quote: You do not want your wife to be violated by another through adultery; do not commit adultery with another man’s wedded wife.
findings.issue: In modern English, a woman being “violated by another” suggests rape or sexual coercion. μοιχευθῆναι specifies adultery with the wife, without specifying coercion. The qualification “through adultery” does not adequately remove the added implication. The same Greek verb is also less transparently represented in the first half than in the reciprocal prohibition.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “You do not want another to commit adultery with your wife; do not commit adultery with another man’s wedded wife.” This changes the English voice while preserving the participants, negations, adultery terminology, and distinction between γυναῖκα and γαμετήν.
